title: Where It Breaks: Diagnosing Perception, Memory, and Decision Failures of a Vision-Language Agent in Pac-Man
abstract: arXiv:2611.06704v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Training an agent to play Pac-Man with only up, down, left and right actions raises a basic question: when performance is poor, what should be improved? Difficulty can arise from reading the screen or from choosing actions over a long sequence. We examine these problems in a Qwen3.5-9B-based agent through separate perception checks and primitive-policy reinforcement-learning studies. In the policy study, which uses textual boards to remove image transcription from the decision interface, completion on eight held-out mazes increased from 0% before this optimization to 80.2% at a selected checkpoint, with three extra lives. The perception checks show that accurate static screenshot reading can coexist with errors during interaction. A separate policy comparison also shows that further optimization can accompany worse action choices. Together, these findings motivate concrete checks for post-training: evaluate perception in use, distinguish

translated_title: 哪里出了问题：诊断视觉-语言智能体在吃豆人游戏中的感知、记忆与决策失败
translated_abstract: 仅用上、下、左、右四个动作训练智能体玩吃豆人提出了一个基本问题：当表现不佳时，应该改进什么？困难可能来自读取屏幕，也可能来自在长序列中选择动作。我们通过对一个基于Qwen3.5-9B的智能体开展独立的感知检查和基元策略强化学习研究来考察这些问题。在策略研究中，我们使用文本棋盘将图像转录从决策接口中移除，八个留出迷宫的通关率从优化前的0%提升到选定检查点时的80.2%（附带三条额外生命）。感知检查表明，准确的静态截图读取可能与交互过程中的错误并存。另一项策略比较也显示，进一步的优化可能伴随更差的动作选择。这些发现共同为后训练提供了具体的检查方法：在使用中评估感知、区分（摘要在此处截断）……
tldr: 该研究通过对基于Qwen3.5-9B的吃豆人智能体分别进行感知检查和使用文本棋盘的基元策略强化学习，发现静态截图读取准确可能与交互中的错误并存、策略优化可能伴随更差的动作选择，从而为后训练提出了在使用中评估感知、区分感知与决策失败的具体检查方法。
en_tdlr: By separately probing perception and training a primitive policy on textual boards for a Qwen3.5-9B Pac-Man agent, raising held-out maze completion from 0% to 80.2%, this work shows that accurate static screenshot reading can coexist with interaction-time errors and further optimization can accompany worse action choices, motivating concrete post-training checks that evaluate perception in use and disentangle perception from decision failures.
